report_name: Miasma and Hades Worms Continue Supply Chain Attacks on npm and PyPI

threat_actors.name: TeamPCP
threat_actors.description: A financially motivated threat actor group attributed to the Miasma and Hades worm campaign targeting open-source ecosystems like npm and PyPI to harvest developer credentials.
threat_actors.goals: Harvest developer credentials at scale for financial gain.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
attack_patterns.description: The Miasma and Hades worms spread by compromising developer accounts and using the stolen credentials to publish new malicious packages or update existing ones in the npm and PyPI repositories.

attack_patterns.name: Event Triggered Execution
attack_patterns.description: The Hades worm uses a `*-setup.pth` file, a path configuration file processed by Python on startup, to automatically execute its malicious payload whenever the developer's Python interpreter starts.

attack_patterns.name: Unsecured Credentials
attack_patterns.description: The worms' payload scours developer machines for unsecured credentials stored in environment variables and configuration files like .npmrc and .git-credentials, as well as SSH keys.

attack_patterns.name: Transfer Data to Cloud Account
attack_patterns.description: Stolen credentials, including API tokens for npm, PyPI, and GitHub, were exfiltrated by publishing them to new, attacker-controlled GitHub repositories.

malware.name: Miasma
malware.description: A self-propagating worm targeting the npm open-source ecosystem to harvest developer credentials and spread to new packages.

malware.name: Hades
malware.description: A self-propagating worm targeting the PyPI open-source ecosystem. It uses `*-setup.pth` files for persistence and execution, harvests developer credentials, and exfiltrates them to GitHub.

tools.name: Bun
tools.description: The Bun JavaScript runtime was fetched and executed by the Hades worm to run its primary malicious logic for credential harvesting and exfiltration.

identities.name: npm
identities.description: The npm open-source package registry, which was targeted by the Miasma worm.

identities.name: PyPI
identities.description: The Python Package Index (PyPI) open-source repository, which was targeted by the Hades worm.

identities.name: GitHub
identities.description: The GitHub platform was abused by the attackers to exfiltrate stolen developer credentials by publishing them to attacker-controlled repositories.

infrastructure.name: GitHub Exfiltration Repositories
infrastructure.description: Attacker-controlled GitHub repositories used to receive exfiltrated developer credentials from systems compromised by the Hades and Miasma worms.

indicators.name: Hades Worm Persistence via .pth File
indicators.pattern:
title: Hades Worm Persistence via .pth File
id: e1c2a3b4-d5e6-4f7a-8b9c-0d1e2f3a4b5c
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of a .pth file containing executable code, a technique used by the Hades worm for persistence in Python environments. Legitimate .pth files should only contain paths.
references:
  - https://securityboulevard.com/2026/07/the-streak-continues-four-more-supply-chain-attacks-hit-npm-and-pypi/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-22
tags:
  - attack.t1546
  - attack.persistence
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '-setup.pth'
    TargetFilename|contains: '\site-packages\'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Unlikely, but some niche packages might use a similar naming convention.
indicators.description: Detects the creation of a `*-setup.pth` file in a Python `site-packages` directory, a persistence method used by the Hades worm.

indicators.name: Anomalous Bun Execution by Hades Worm
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Bun Execution by Hades Worm
id: a2b3c4d5-e6f7-4a8b-9c0d-1e2f3a4b5c6d
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of the Bun JavaScript runtime (bun.exe), which may be anomalous in some environments. The Hades worm was observed fetching and using Bun to execute its payload.
references:
  - https://securityboulevard.com/2026/07/the-streak-continues-four-more-supply-chain-attacks-hit-npm-and-pypi/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-22
tags:
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.execution
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\bun.exe'
  filter_legit_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\explorer.exe'
      - '\code.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit_parent
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate use of the Bun runtime by developers. The rule is tuned to detect execution by non-interactive or unexpected parent processes.
indicators.description: Detects the execution of `bun.exe`, a tool leveraged by the Hades worm, which may be anomalous in environments where it is not standard developer tooling.

indicators.name: Hades Worm Component 'bun.exe'
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Hades Worm Component 'bun.exe' File Creation
id: b3c4d5e6-f7a8-4b9c-0d1e-2f3a4b5c6d7e
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of 'bun.exe', a legitimate tool abused by the Hades worm. Its presence may be anomalous.
references:
  - https://securityboulevard.com/2026/07/the-streak-continues-four-more-supply-chain-attacks-hit-npm-and-pypi/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-22
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
  - attack.initial_access
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\bun.exe'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate installation of the Bun runtime.
indicators.description: Detects the presence of the file `bun.exe`, a legitimate tool that was downloaded and used by the Hades worm.

indicators.name: Potential Credential Exfiltration to GitHub
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Credential Exfiltration to GitHub
id: c4d5e6f7-a8b9-4c0d-1e2f-3a4b5c6d7e8f
status: experimental
description: Detects potentially anomalous network connections to api.github.com, particularly from non-interactive processes, which could indicate credential exfiltration as seen with the Hades worm.
references:
  - https://securityboulevard.com/2026/07/the-streak-continues-four-more-supply-chain-attacks-hit-npm-and-pypi/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-22
tags:
  - attack.t1537
  - attack.exfiltration
level: low
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationHostname: 'api.github.com'
    Initiated: 'true'
  filter:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\git.exe'
      - '\gh.exe'
      - '\Code.exe'
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate tools and scripts interacting with the GitHub API. This rule requires significant tuning for a specific environment.
indicators.description: Detects anomalous network traffic to `api.github.com` from processes other than legitimate Git clients or web browsers, which could be indicative of credential exfiltration.
